newsitem.title: USA: Abraxas sees Q4 above analysts' estimates.
newsitem.headline: Abraxas sees Q4 above analysts' estimates.

text.p: Abraxas Petroleum Corp said Wednesday it expects fourth quarter 1996 earnings to exceed analysts' estimates.
The company said it expects net income applicable to common stock for the fourth quarter of 1996 to be at least $1.6 million, or $0.28 per primary share.
It noted the average estimate published by First Call Corporate Monitor is for a loss of $0.19 per share.
Abraxas said it expects cash flow from operations, before working capital and after preferred dividends, to exceed $6.8 million, or $1.17 primary share.
It noted these are preliminary figures and subject to a year-end audit. Final results are expected by mid-March.
"Our acquisition of the Wamsutter/Wyoming property positively impacted fourth quarter results for the full period," said chief executive Robert L. G. Watson explained.

"Other acquisitions made during the quarter -- CGGS in Canada, the Portilla/Happy Fields and the East White Point/Stedman Island Fields in south Texas -- contributed to less than half of the quarter's results.

"Equivalent average daily production more than tripled to 10,400 barrels up from 3,327 equivalent barrels in the 1995 fourth quarter and our December 1996 exit rate was 14,100 equivalent barrels per day."

"Additionally, higher commodity prices bolstered our results," Watson said. "We realized average prices of $22.31/barrel for oil, $2.00/mcf for natural gas and $15.40/barrel for natural gas liquids during the quarter. Comparable prices reported in 1995 were $16.97/barrel, $1.63/mcf and $10.54/barrel respectively."
